note: Add Content by Bundle provides exactly one Views area handler (id add_content_by_bundle, registered via hook_views_data on views.add_content_by_bundle). It has no configure route (configure=null), no permissions, no Drush, and no plugin types. Its only persistent state lives inside a view's config at display.<display>.display_options.<header|footer>.add_content_by_bundle, with keys type (entity type), bundle (plain-string bundle machine name), label, class, target ('' | tray | modal), width, destination, params, login_redirect, group, form_mode. All medium/hard cases are grounded in that real view config: introspection reads back a view's configured target bundle / dialog target; execution adds or reconfigures the area handler and is verified against the live views.view.* config.

evals.prompt: In Drupal, the add_content_by_bundle module lets me put an 'add content' link on a view. Where in the view do I add it, and what is the Views handler/area called?
evals.expected_output: It is a Views area handler (id add_content_by_bundle). You add it to a view display's Header or Footer via the Views UI ('Add Content by Bundle link'), then choose the entity type, bundle, label, class and target.

evals.prompt: With the add_content_by_bundle Views area, how do I make the 'add content' link open the entity add form in a modal dialog instead of a full page, and can I set the dialog width?
evals.expected_output: Set the area's 'target' option to 'modal' (or 'tray' for off-canvas). The link then gets the use-ajax class and data-dialog-type=modal, and the 'width' option controls the dialog width in pixels (default 600).

evals.prompt: Which entity types can the add_content_by_bundle Views area link to, and which route does it use for a node content type?
evals.expected_output: For nodes it uses the node.add route (node_type = bundle). It also supports taxonomy terms (entity.taxonomy_term.add_form), ECK entities (eck.entity.add), Group content, and any entity type via its add-form/add-page link template.

evals.prompt: This site has a view with machine name 'acbb_known' that includes an Add Content by Bundle link in its footer. Inspect the live view configuration and state which entity type and bundle the link is configured to create.
evals.expected_output: The footer's add_content_by_bundle handler targets entity type 'node' and bundle 'article' (in views.view.acbb_known display.default.display_options.footer.add_content_by_bundle: type: node, bundle: article, label 'Add ACBB Known').

evals.prompt: The view 'acbb_modal_known' on this site has an Add Content by Bundle footer link that opens the add form in a dialog. Inspect the live configuration and state whether it opens as a modal or an off-canvas tray, and what dialog width is configured.
evals.expected_output: It opens as a modal (target: modal) with width 850, per views.view.acbb_modal_known display.default.display_options.footer.add_content_by_bundle.

evals.prompt: This site has a view with machine name 'acbb_task' whose default display has an empty footer. Using the add_content_by_bundle module, add an Add Content by Bundle link to that view's footer that creates a node of the 'page' (Basic page) content type. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: The default display footer of views.view.acbb_task gains an add_content_by_bundle handler with type: node and bundle: page (e.g. set display_options.footer.add_content_by_bundle via config or the Views UI and save).

evals.prompt: The view 'acbb_tray' on this site already has an Add Content by Bundle footer link that currently opens the add form as a normal full page. Reconfigure it so the add form instead opens in an off-canvas (off-screen) tray, and apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: In views.view.acbb_tray the add_content_by_bundle footer handler has target set to 'tray' (off-canvas), giving the link data-dialog-renderer=off_canvas.
